inputs.content:
# Onsoo Botanicals: US market entry — briefing pack

> **Synthetic benchmark data.** The company, people, competitors and every figure in this pack are fictional. They were generated for a reasoning benchmark and are internally consistent, but they are not real market data.

## 1. Context

Onsoo Botanicals is a Seoul-based skincare company founded in 2011. FY2025 revenue was KRW 184.0 billion
(about $133M at KRW 1,380 per dollar) with an operating margin of 11.2%. Sales split: Korea 58%, Japan 24%,
Southeast Asia 18%. The best-selling product is the Rice Ferment Barrier Cream (50 ml), 31% of revenue.
Onsoo has no US entity today; since January 2026 a cross-border seller has listed three Onsoo SKUs on
Amazon US as a test.

**Decision maker:** CEO Park Ji-won, with the board, at the March 2027 board meeting.

## 2. Decision question

**Should Onsoo enter the US market in 2027, and if so, by which route?**

## 3. Objectives and constraints (set by the board)

- **Ambition:** build a US business "on the way to $40M revenue by 2030".
- **Investment cap:** cumulative US cash outflow (peak negative cumulative cash) of no more than $18M through 2030.
- **Payback:** cumulative US cash flow back to zero within four years of launch, i.e. by the end of 2030.
- **Group margin floor:** group operating margin at or above 8% in every year.
- **Bandwidth:** management can run only one major new-market launch in 2027 (the US, or a Japan scale-up).

## 4. Current views inside the company

- **CEO (initial hypothesis):** "Launch in the US in 2027 through Amazon, then add specialty beauty retail
  from 2029 once Amazon sales pass $10M and aided awareness passes 15%."
- **Independent board member (former retail executive):** "Amazon alone will never get us to $40M. A national
  specialty-retail launch in 600 doors in 2027 is how every big K-beauty brand built awareness."
- **Head of Japan:** "Japan is the safer use of 2027: we know the market and the retailers."

The planning team has modeled the Amazon-led route (Option A), the retail-led route (Option B) and a Japan
scale-up (Option J). Their inputs are below; they did not draw a conclusion.

## 5. Market data

**Table 1. US facial skincare sales, $ billions**

|  | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| All facial skincare | 20.1 | 21.3 | 22.6 | 23.5 | 24.5 |
| of which K-beauty brands | 1.9 | 2.3 | 2.7 | 3.1 | 3.6 |

**Table 2. Where US consumers bought K-beauty skincare, 2025, share of sales**

| Channel | Share |
|---|---|
| Amazon | 41% |
| Specialty beauty retail | 27% |
| Mass retail | 14% |
| Brand websites (DTC) | 12% |
| Other | 6% |

## 6. Amazon pilot (January–June 2026, three SKUs, cross-border seller)

**Table 3. Pilot units sold per month**

| Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7,400 | 8,600 | 10,100 | 11,800 | 12,900 | 14,000 | 64,800 |

- Average selling price: $24.00 per unit. Advertising cost of sales (ACoS, Amazon ad spend as a share of
  Amazon sales) over the pilot: 28%.
- Ratings: 4.5 stars from 2,140 reviews. The most common complaint (6% of reviews): some units carried
  Korean-only label text.
- 90-day repeat purchase rate: 29% of first-time buyers. Benchmarks: 31% for skincare brands in their first
  year on Amazon US (agency data); 48% for Onsoo in Korea.

## 7. Unit economics inputs (Rice Ferment Barrier Cream, per unit)

**Table 4. Per-unit inputs by channel, US dollars**

| Item | Amazon | Specialty retail |
|---|---|---|
| Consumer price | $24.00 | $28.00 (shelf) |
| Price Onsoo receives | $24.00 | $14.00 (wholesale = 50% of shelf price) |
| Amazon referral fee | 15% of price | — |
| Amazon fulfillment (FBA) fee | $5.10 | — |
| Ex-factory product cost | $3.50 | $3.50 |
| Freight to the US warehouse or retailer DC | $0.55 | $0.75 |
| US import duty | 15% of ex-factory cost | 15% of ex-factory cost |
| Retailer co-op marketing allowance | — | 8% of wholesale |
| Returns and damages allowance | — | 4% of wholesale |
| Advertising | ACoS × price | in fixed marketing budget |

The planning team applies the hero product's per-unit economics to all SKUs. Working capital: the planning team holds four months of landed product cost (ex-factory + freight + duty) as inventory.

## 8. Planning-team forecasts by option

**Table 5. Volume forecasts, units**

| Option | 2027 | 2028 | 2029 | 2030 | Key assumptions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A · Amazon-led: Amazon units | 300,000 | 560,000 | 850,000 | 1,100,000 | Four more SKUs from 2027; ACoS 25% (planning team: ACoS falls as the brand matures) |
| B · Retail-led: specialty-retail doors | 600 | 600 | 800 | 1,000 | 4.5 units per door per week (from the retailer's deck on successful newcomer brands) |
| B · Retail-led: Amazon units | 390,000 | 728,000 | 1,105,000 | 1,430,000 | Option A volumes × 1.3 (awareness halo from retail); ACoS 25% |

**Table 6. Fixed and one-time US costs, $ millions**

| Cost | Option A | Option B |
|---|---|---|
| Compliance (MoCRA registration, safety substantiation, labeling), insurance — per year | 0.5 | 0.5 |
| US team — per year | 0.9 | 0.9 |
| Off-Amazon brand marketing (influencers, social) — per year | 0.7 | 0.7 |
| National retail marketing and sampling — per year | — | 6.0 |
| Field sales and merchandising team — per year | — | 1.5 |
| Setup: entity, registration, labels — one-time, 2027 | 0.8 | 0.8 |
| Retailer launch fee — one-time, 2027 | — | 0.5 |
| In-store fixtures — one-time per new door | — | $1,100 per door |

**Table 7. Option J · Japan scale-up instead of the US in 2027**

|  | 2027 | 2028 | 2029 | 2030 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Incremental revenue, $M | 2.5 | 4.5 | 6.0 | 7.0 |
| Contribution margin on that revenue | 30% | 30% | 30% | 30% |
| Added fixed cost, $M per year | 0.8 | 0.8 | 0.8 | 0.8 |
| One-time cost, $M | 1.0 | — | — | — |

Japan facial skincare grows about 1.5% a year; Onsoo already holds a 3.1% share there.

**Group context.** Excluding the US, the group plans revenue of $140M (2027), $146M (2028), $152M (2029) and
$158M (2030) at an operating margin of 11.0%.

## 9. Retail evidence

**Table 8. First-year sell-through of newcomer skincare brands in US specialty beauty retail**

| Brand's aided awareness among category buyers | Median units per door per week | Interquartile range |
|---|---|---|
| Below 10% | 2.6 | 1.9–3.4 |
| 10–20% | 3.5 | 2.8–4.3 |
| Above 20% | 4.6 | 3.9–5.5 |

Source: a retail analytics firm, 2025, 46 brands. The leading specialty retailer reviews newcomer brands after
12 months and removes brands selling below 4.0 units per door per week.

## 10. Customer evidence

Survey, September 2026, 1,200 US women aged 18–44 who bought facial skincare in the last six months:

- Aided awareness of Onsoo: 4% of all respondents; 9% among K-beauty buyers.
- 61% of K-beauty buyers say they buy K-beauty on Amazon most often; 22% at specialty beauty retail.
- 38% of K-beauty buyers discovered their last new brand on TikTok; 17% in a store.
- 52% of respondents who tried a K-beauty product said "price compared with US brands" was a reason.

## 11. Competitor evidence

**Table 9. K-beauty brands that entered the US recently (public reporting and interviews)**

| Brand | Entry route | Outcome by 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Mooncrest | Retail-first 2023, 450 doors | Removed from shelves in 2025; estimated cumulative US loss $21M |
| Saebom | Amazon-first 2022 | About $30M US revenue in 2025; added 300 retail doors in 2025 |
| Gaon Lab | Amazon-first 2022 | Below $5M US revenue in 2025 |
| Yeoreum | Amazon-first 2023 | Below $5M US revenue in 2025 |

Agency benchmark: for skincare brands scaling from $5M to $20M a year on Amazon US, median ACoS is 32%
(range 26%–38%); ad costs per click rise as brands bid on broader keywords.

## 12. Other material circulated to the board

- A trade-press article (2026) reports that "the US K-beauty market reached $5.2 billion in 2025". The article's
  figure covers skincare, makeup and hair care sold by Korean brands.
- The independent board member's memo: "Across 30 K-beauty brands sold in the US, the number of specialty-retail
  doors a brand is in correlates with its Amazon sales (correlation 0.71). Retail drives Amazon sales; that is where
  the 1.3× halo in Option B comes from."

## 13. Uncertainties

- **Tariff:** the US is reviewing the duty on cosmetics imported from Korea; a rise from 15% to 25% is possible,
  with a decision expected in mid-2027.
- **Advertising cost at scale:** the pilot ran at 28% ACoS on a small budget.
- **Repeat purchase:** US repeat is below Korea's; it is unclear whether it rises with more SKUs.
- **FX:** product costs are in won; a weaker won lowers dollar costs.

storyline.governing_thought: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail: only this route fits the board's limits, but it pays back by 2030 only if ad cost stays near the pilot's 28%

exec_summary.text: The US deserves Onsoo's one 2027 launch: K-beauty skincare grows fast, mostly on Amazon

sub_points.text: K-beauty skincare grew 17% a year in 2021–25, against 5% for the market
Pilot units nearly doubled in five months, with repeat near the US benchmark

exec_summary.text: National retail fails the board's tests even on the planning team's own, optimistic inputs

sub_points.text: Cumulative cash reaches −$20.8M by 2030; group margin falls to 4.5% in 2027
At today's awareness, newcomers sell 2.6 units per door a week, below the 4.0 cut-off

exec_summary.text: On planning inputs, Amazon-led entry alone passes every test, yet reaches two-thirds of the $40M ambition

sub_points.text: Peak outflow is $1.9M against the $18M cap; group margin stays above 9%
Japan also passes but adds $7.0M of revenue in 2030, against $26.4M

exec_summary.text: Ad cost decides the payback: it holds only below an average ACoS of about 28.6%

sub_points.text: At the 32% median for scaling brands, cash is still −$2.3M at end-2030; a 25% duty also breaks it

exec_summary.text: Launch with five gates, and add specialty retail only once awareness passes 20%, not 15%

sub_points.text: If ad cost or repeat misses its end-2027 gate, hold US spend and bring the Japan scale-up forward

next_steps.action: Approve Amazon-led US entry, the five launch gates and a restated 2030 revenue goal
Set up the US entity, MoCRA registration and US-English labels; move the pilot SKUs to Onsoo's own Amazon account
Launch the four new SKUs and track ACoS, repeat and aided awareness monthly
Re-plan prices and ad budget once the US duty decision is known
Hold the end-2027 gate review: scale up, hold spend, or bring the Japan scale-up forward

constraints.item: Investment cap: peak cumulative US outflow no more than $18M through 2030
constraints.effect: Route A peaks at −$1.9M (plan), −$2.4M (pilot ACoS) and −$3.2M (32% ACoS); route B reaches −$20.8M and fails

constraints.item: Payback: cumulative US cash back to zero by end-2030
constraints.effect: Route A passes at 25% and 28% ACoS but fails at 32% or with a 25% duty; the governing thought and exec item 4 state the condition

constraints.item: Group operating margin at least 8% every year
constraints.effect: Route A keeps group margin above 9% in every case tested; route B drops it to 4.5% in 2027

constraints.item: Bandwidth: one major new-market launch in 2027
constraints.effect: Choosing the US defers the Japan scale-up; it stays the fallback at the end-2027 gate

constraints.item: Amazon ad cost at scale: agency median 32% (26%–38%) against the planning team's 25%
constraints.effect: Section 4 is built on it; the payback holds only below about 28.6% average ACoS

constraints.item: Possible US duty rise from 15% to 25% (decision mid-2027)
constraints.effect: Adds $0.35 a unit and lowers break-even ACoS to about 27.1%; at the pilot's ACoS the payback then fails

constraints.item: Working capital: four months of landed cost held as inventory
constraints.effect: Deducted in every cash figure; $1.7M at end-2030 for route A
Covered by setup cost; gate 1 before launch

alternatives.option: Japan scale-up in 2027 instead of the US (Head of Japan)
alternatives.why: Passes every board test, but adds $7.0M of revenue in 2030 against $26.4M for route A and builds no US position; route A's downside stays within 18% of the cash cap. Kept as the fallback if the end-2027 gates fail

alternatives.option: A smaller retail-led launch with fewer doors
alternatives.why: Retail marketing and field costs ($7.5M a year) do not scale with doors; covering them needs more than 4,200 doors

alternatives.option: CEO's plan: Amazon in 2027, specialty retail from 2029 at 15% awareness and $10M Amazon sales
alternatives.why: Sequence kept; trigger raised to 20% awareness because brands at 10–20% sell 3.5 units, below the 4.0 cut-off, and retail sized so the 2030 payback holds

failure_threshold.driver: average Amazon ACoS 2027–30 (and, second, Amazon volumes)
failure_threshold.threshold: above about 28.6% average ACoS (27.1% if the duty rises to 25% from 2028) the 2030 payback fails; at the pilot's 28%, a volume shortfall above about 4% also breaks it
failure_threshold.range: cumulative US cash at end-2030: low −$2.3M (32% ACoS) / base +$0.4M (pilot 28%) / high +$2.4M (planning team 25%)

consistency.headline: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail: only this route fits the board's limits, but it pays back by 2030 only if ad cost stays near the pilot's 28%
consistency.fix: The governing thought and exec item 4 state the ad-cost condition instead of claiming a 2030 payback; exec item 3 names the planning-team inputs and the gap to the $40M ambition
